identity.title: Global Agent Single Source of Truth
identity.summary: This XML document is the optimized source of truth for shared agent behavior across repos.

compatibility.markdown-wrapper: Keep AGENTS.md as the compatibility entrypoint for adapters, tests, and tools that still expect Markdown.

load-order.step: If the current repo contains .agents/repo.md, read it as the repo-specific supplement.
Load only the relevant files from contexts/.
Load only the relevant capsule from capsules/ when a task-class operating pack is required.
Load any invoked command docs from commands/.
Load only the needed reusable rule cards from rules/common/.
Load only relevant skill docs from skills/.
Load adapter-specific files only when the active toolchain requires them.

command-rules.rule: Command definitions in commands/**/*.md are authoritative.
If a command name exists in commands/, including namespaced command files such as commands/gsd/*.md, follow that file exactly.

If the user sends a slash-style command such as /cm, /prime, /plan-feature, /execute, /optimize-prompt, or /gsd:help, first look for a matching command document in commands/ before treating it as plain text.

Treat underscore and hyphen variants of the same slash-style workflow command as equivalent when they resolve to one unambiguous command file. Prefer the on-disk file name as canonical when reporting or persisting command names.
Treat gsd <subcommand>, gsd-<subcommand>, and /gsd:<subcommand> as equivalent requests for commands/gsd/<subcommand>.md. If the subcommand is omitted, route to commands/gsd/help.md.
When the intended command name is ambiguous, check commands/ for the closest matching command file and use that as the first resolution step.
Do not invent command behavior when a command doc exists.

skill-rules.rule: If a skill is explicitly requested, load its SKILL.md before acting.
If multiple skills apply, use the minimal set and state the order.

repo-supplement-rules.rule: Repo root AGENTS.md may be a symlink to this global file.
Repo-specific instructions belong in .agents/repo.md inside the repo.
Repo supplements extend global rules unless they explicitly state otherwise.

context-rules.rule: contexts/ is the canonical workspace state layer for reusable planning and execution context.
Load only the minimum context files needed for the task instead of bulk-loading the whole directory.
contexts/decisions.md is the source of truth for locked decisions, deferred ideas, and open questions.
The current project's .agents/contexts/state.md is the live source of truth for resumable workflow state.
The current project's .agents/contexts/research-index.md is the live index for reusable research artifacts.
The current project's .agents/contexts/session-index.md is the live index for resumable work sessions.
Tracked contexts/state.md, contexts/research-index.md, and contexts/session-index.md in this repo are shared compatibility documents, not live per-project runtime files.
contexts/tooling.md is the source of truth for detected environment tooling defaults.
contexts/verification.md is the source of truth for available automated checks and preferred verification order.
contexts/artifacts.md is the source of truth for resumable artifact retrieval priorities.
contexts/agent-catalog.md is the source of truth for workflow expert agents, their triggers, and routing boundaries.
contexts/ui-ux.md is required before substantial design-heavy UI work.
contexts/user-taste.md is the source of truth for durable user-specific output preferences and dislikes.
contexts/reference-library.md is the source of truth for approved references, exemplars, and inspiration inputs.

capsule-rules.rule: capsules/ contains task-class operating packs that combine context assembly, examples, anti-patterns, critics, graders, and learning policies.
Use a capsule when the task is substantial enough that better context assembly and critique would materially change the outcome.
Skills provide reusable know-how; capsules provide reusable execution and learning behavior.
Load only the capsule required for the task class instead of bulk-loading the entire directory.
For substantial creative or API workflow tasks, select a capsule before planning or implementation.

rule-card-rules.rule: Reusable workflow policy should live in rules/common/ instead of being duplicated across prompts and commands.
Rule cards extend the system prompt; they do not replace task-specific command or skill instructions.
Use the prompt optimization routing rule before ambiguous, multi-step, handoff-oriented, or substantial tasks, especially before defaulting into RPI.
Use the output-quality gate rule before substantial creative work or API work where specificity and non-generic output matter.
Use the learning-loop rule after explicit user correction, critic rejection, or eval failure.
Use the expert-agent routing rule before delegating substantial workflow tasks to specialist agents.
Use the package-manager detection rule before presenting or running Node package-manager commands in an unknown repo.
Use the verification automation rule before recommending automated checks in a repo with scripts or build tooling.
Use the artifact retrieval rule before loading multiple workflow artifacts into context.
Use the model routing rule before spawning subagents to select the optimal model tier based on task complexity, budget, and CLI context.
Prefer the lowest capable model for delegated bounded work when it can complete the task without degrading correctness or safety.

adapter-rules.rule: adapters/ contains provider-specific operational assets such as hooks, statuslines, and settings helpers.
Provider adapters must not redefine canonical workflow policy that belongs in prompts/, contexts/, commands/, or rules/common/.
Compatibility wrappers under hooks/ may delegate to adapter files, but adapter files are the maintained implementation.

session-rules.rule: Use project-local .agents/sessions/ for ordinary workflow continuity across sessions.
Treat the current project's .agents/contexts/state.md and .agents/contexts/session-index.md as the live continuity source of truth.
Use handoffs when work is being intentionally transferred or compacted for another agent.
Keep handoffs under thoughts/shared/handoffs/ as shared transfer artifacts, not as the normal session path.
Session artifacts should summarize current position, active artifacts, blockers, and the next recommended command.

expert-agent-rules.rule: Prefer narrow workflow experts over broad persona agents when the task is about continuity, parity, workflow gating, eval design, or tool integration.
Load contexts/agent-catalog.md before introducing or routing to new workflow experts.
Use the smallest expert set that covers the task cleanly.
Stay local when the request is a narrow operational fix rather than workflow-system work.
Prefer subagents and skills for bounded, parallelizable, or low-risk work so the main context window stays focused on the critical path.
Delegate extraction, search, summarization, formatting, verification, and other narrowly scoped subtasks by default when they can be expressed without shared hidden context.
Use node ./scripts/expert-agent-routing-tools.mjs route --input "<task>" when the correct expert is not obvious from the request.

non-negotiables.rule: Prefer repo scripts over shell aliases or functions for execution.
Ask for clarification when intent is ambiguous.
For risky or destructive actions, require explicit confirmation.
When reporting artifact locations, generated files, handoffs, plans, research notes, sessions, or workflow outputs to the user, always include the absolute filesystem path.
Prefer absolute filesystem paths in command outputs, skill outputs, and all research to plan to implement to validate workflow updates.
